I've reviewed every plausible location. Findings:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — copy/sublicence/reverse-engineering limits tied to the licensed Work only; ordinary licence-scope, not a field-of-use or market restriction.
- **§ 2 (Grant)** — non-exclusive licence to Sparkling; no exclusivity or purchase commitment binding us.
- **§ 19** — mutual non-solicit of employees, not a non-compete (and mutual, so not this rule).
- **§ 20 / Page 10 general matters, § 14 confidentiality** — no covenant limiting Sparkling's businesses, products or sourcing. Text searches for "compet", "exclusive", "develop", "Sparkling shall not" and "business" surface nothing restricting our commercial activity.

No restriction on Sparkling's business exists, which is the preferred position — no redline needed.

input.quote: (e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Sparkling, which meets the preferred position (no restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build). Section 3 "Restrictions on Use" is confined to ordinary licence-scope controls over the licensed Work (no copying beyond backup, no sublicence/transfer, no reverse engineering, no use outside the licence grant); it does not limit what products Sparkling may procure, develop or market, and does not bar dealings with Garman's competitors. Section 2 grants a non-exclusive licence with no minimum purchase or exclusivity commitment, and Section 19 is a mutual employee non-solicit rather than a non-compete (and being reciprocal, it is out of scope for this rule). Searches for "compet", "exclusive", "develop" and "Sparkling shall not" across the document return no covenant restricting our commercial activity, and the general matters provisions (Section 20 and the Page 10 sub-clauses) contain only standard boilerplate. No redline required.
